script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for February 11. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Summer and winter, spring and fall—we take seasons for granted.  But they exist only because Earth is tilted.  Just 23.

Earth's axis is tilted 23.5 degrees relative to its orbit. During summer, your hemisphere tilts toward the Sun—sunlight hits more directly and the days are longer. During winter, you tilt away—sunlight comes at an angle and days are shorter. When the Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, the Southern tilts away.  That's why Australia has Christmas in summer while Canada has it in winter.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: A small tilt—just 23. 5 degrees—creates the difference between life and death, harvest and famine, growth and dormancy.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Life Seasons - Recognize Your Cycle.

Here's your activity: Consider: are you in a spring (new growth), summer (abundance), fall (harvesting), or winter (rest/dormancy) in different areas of your life? Name them. Each season has its purpose—honor where you are. This helps you identify what 'season' you're in personally and professionally.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why seasons change can be applied to life seasons - recognize your cycle. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
